newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Permanent says prospects for 1996 good.
newsitem.headline: Irish Permanent says prospects for 1996 good.

text.p: Irish financial services group Irish Permanent Plc said on Tuesday it was well positioned to take advantage of increasing demand in the Irish market in 1996.
"The Irish Permanent is well positioned to benefit from an economic and demographic environment favourable to retail financial services," chief executive Roy Douglas said in a results statement.

In particular, the company was poised to benefit from the recovery of mortgage lending in the U.K. market, following the group's acquisition last year of centralised mortgage lender Capital Home Loans Ltd, Douglas said.

The group, which announced a pre-tax profit for 1996 of 48.6 million Irish pounds - up 14.7 percent on 1995 - said increased profitability reflected growth in its loan portfolio and a strong performance by the Group Treasury, combined with growth in non-interest income and cost containment.

Looking ahead, the group said, expansion of its card customer base - currently in excess of 100,000 card-holders - was an important aspect of broadening its relationships with the personal banking customer.
It would continue to develop its penetration of the money transmission markets, Irish Permanent said.
